proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(\vartheta\) in either full fiber.  By the definition of \(r\) and selected-table positivity,
\[
r_e=\sum_{w,z}p_{ewz}>0\qquad(e\in\mathcal E).
\]
The definition \(c=P_{\vartheta}(S=1)>0\) and the identity
\(P_{\vartheta}(E=e\mid S=1)=r_e\) give
\[
P_{\vartheta}(E=e,S=1)
=P_{\vartheta}(S=1)P_{\vartheta}(E=e\mid S=1)
=c r_e>0.
\]
Since \(\{E=e,S=1\}\subseteq\{E=e\}\), monotonicity of probability yields
\[
m_e=P_{\vartheta}(E=e)\ge P_{\vartheta}(E=e,S=1)=c r_e>0.
\]
In design A the equality \(P_{\vartheta}(E)=m\) is part of the definition of \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\), so a nonempty fiber forces the supplied \(m\) to be in \(\Delta_{\mathcal E}^{\circ}\).  In design B, \(m\) denotes the margin induced by \(P_{\vartheta}\), and the same calculation proves that every one of its coordinates is positive.

We prove both directions and retain boundary cases throughout.

First let \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_A(p,m)\).  The preceding lemma gives \(m_e>0\).  Because
\[
P_{\vartheta}(E=e,S=1)=c r_e>0,
\]
conditioning on \(E=e\) is legitimate.  Outcome-dependent selection implies that the conditional law of \((U,W,Z)\) given \((E=e,S=1)\) is its conditional law given \(E=e\).  Define
\[
a_{ei}(z)=P_{\vartheta}(U=i,Z=z\mid E=e),
\qquad
b_i(w)=\text{the normalized proxy kernel for type }i\text{ in }\vartheta.
\]
For \(\pi_i>0\) this kernel equals \(P_{\vartheta}(W=w\mid U=i)\); unlike that conditional notation, the mechanism kernel remains defined when \(\pi_i=0\).
Response consistency makes \(a_{ei}=0\) unless \(i\in\mathcal I_e\).  Proxy exclusion gives, for \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\),
\[
T_e(w,z)
=P_{\vartheta}(W=w,Z=z\mid E=e,S=1)
=b_i(w)a_{ei}(z)+b_j(w)a_{ej}(z).
\]
Summing this identity over \(w\), and using \(\sum_w b_i(w)=\sum_wb_j(w)=1\), gives
\[
a_{ei}(z)+a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z).
\]
Thus \((b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\).  Moreover, since \(E=11\) occurs exactly for types \(1,2\) and \(E=00\) exactly for types \(2,4\),
\[
P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=1,Y=1)=\sum_z a_{11,2}(z),
\qquad
P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=0,Y=0)=\sum_z a_{00,2}(z).
\]
Hence \(\tau(\vartheta)=\tau_C(b,a)\).

Conversely, take \((b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\).  Nonemptiness of \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\), together with the preceding lemma, supplies \(m_e>0\).  For every response type define
\[
h_i(z)=\sum_{e:i\in\mathcal I_e}m_ea_{ei}(z),
\qquad
\pi_i=\sum_z h_i(z).
\]
Because \(a_{ei}\ge0\), all these quantities are nonnegative.  Also
\[
\sum_i\pi_i
=\sum_e m_e\sum_z\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_e}a_{ei}(z)
=\sum_e m_e\sum_zv_e(z)
=\sum_e m_e=1.
\]
If \(\pi_i>0\), put \(g_i(z)=h_i(z)/\pi_i\); if \(\pi_i=0\), choose any probability vector \(g_i\).  Let \(e_1(i)\) and \(e_0(i)\) be the unique incident cells of type \(i\) having treatment coordinates one and zero, respectively.  When \(h_i(z)>0\), set
\[
e_i(z)=\frac{m_{e_1(i)}a_{e_1(i),i}(z)}{h_i(z)}.
\]
The numerator lies between zero and \(h_i(z)\), so \(e_i(z)\in[0,1]\).  When \(h_i(z)=0\), set \(e_i(z)=0\).  Nonnegativity and \(m_e>0\) then imply that both incident terms \(m_ea_{ei}(z)\) vanish, so this convention preserves
\[
\pi_i g_i(z)e_i(z)=m_{e_1(i)}a_{e_1(i),i}(z),
\qquad
\pi_i g_i(z)\{1-e_i(z)\}=m_{e_0(i)}a_{e_0(i),i}(z).
\]
Generate \(U,Z,X,Y,W\) using these kernels, the supplied \(b_i\), and \(Y=Y_U(X)\).  The last display and proxy exclusion built into the construction give, for every incident \((e,i)\),
\[
P(U=i,Z=z,E=e,W=w)=m_ea_{ei}(z)b_i(w).
\]
Consequently,
\[
P(E=e,W=w,Z=z)=m_eT_e(w,z),
\qquad P(E=e)=m_e.
\]
Since \(\sum_e r_e(m_e/r_e)=1\), one has \(\min_e(m_e/r_e)\le1\).  Thus
\[
c_0=\frac12\min_e\frac{m_e}{r_e}\in(0,1],
\qquad
s_e=\frac{c_0r_e}{m_e}\in(0,1/2].
\]
Let \(S\mid E=e\) be Bernoulli with success probability \(s_e\).  Then
\[
P(S=1)=\sum_es_em_e=c_0\sum_er_e=c_0
\]
and
\[
P(E=e,W=w,Z=z\mid S=1)
=\frac{s_em_eT_e(w,z)}{c_0}
=r_eT_e(w,z)=p_{ewz}.
\]
This is a legal member of \(\mathcal F_A(p,m)\), and the already proved conditional calculation gives \(\tau=\tau_C\).  The conventions for \(\pi_i=0\), \(h_i(z)=0\), and zero entries of \(b_i\) show explicitly that no interiority of latent mechanisms was used.

For design B, the forward calculation is unchanged.  Instrument exogeneity supplies a common marginal \(g\) and
\[
\sum_{e:i\in\mathcal I_e}m_ea_{ei}(z)
=P_{\vartheta}(U=i,Z=z)=\pi_i g(z).
\]
Observed positivity implies \(P_{\vartheta}(Z=z)>0\), hence \(g\in\Delta_{\mathcal Z}^{\circ}\).  Furthermore \(q^X_z=P_{\vartheta}(X=1,Z=z)\), so the displayed cross-product inequality in \(\mathcal C_B(T)\) is exactly \(Z\not\!\perp X\).  This proves that the forward image lies in \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).

Conversely, start from \((b,a,m,g,\pi)\in\mathcal C_B(T)\).  The shared-
\(Z\) equations say exactly that the preceding \(h_i(z)\) equals \(\pi_i g(z)\).  The same treatment-kernel construction therefore uses the common \(g\), including when \(\pi_i=0\), and produces \(Z\perp U\).  The relevance inequality produces \(Z\not\!\perp X\), while the same selection construction reproduces \(p\).  Hence this is a member of \(\mathcal F_B(p)\) with target \(\tau_C\).  Both maps are therefore onto and target preserving.

Fix a cell \(e\) with \(\mathcal I_e=\{i,j\}\).  Selected-table positivity gives \(v_e(z)>0\), so define its normalized column point
\[
c_{ez}=\frac{T_e(\cdot,z)}{v_e(z)}\in\Delta_{\mathcal W}.
\]
If \(T_e=b_i a_{ei}^{\top}+b_j a_{ej}^{\top}\) has rank two, then \(b_i\ne b_j\) and neither coefficient row is identically zero.  Division by \(v_e(z)=a_{ei}(z)+a_{ej}(z)\) gives
\[
c_{ez}=q_{ez}b_i+(1-q_{ez})b_j,
\qquad
q_{ez}=\frac{a_{ei}(z)}{v_e(z)}\in[0,1].
\]
Thus the two endpoints lie on \(\mathcal L_e\) and the closed segment between them contains every \(c_{ez}\).  Conversely, if distinct \(b_i,b_j\in\mathcal L_e\cap\Delta_{\mathcal W}\) have this segment-containment property, the unique barycentric coordinates \(q_{ez}\in[0,1]\) define
\[
a_{ei}(z)=v_e(z)q_{ez},
\qquad
a_{ej}(z)=v_e(z)(1-q_{ez}),
\]
and reproduce \(T_e\).  This proves the cellwise equivalence without a positivity assumption on the latent coefficients.

Because \(T_e\) has rank two, its normalized column points are not all equal.  Choose a coordinate functional \(h_e\) that is nonconstant on them and put
\[
\alpha_e=\min_z c_{ez}(h_e),
\qquad
\beta_e=\max_z c_{ez}(h_e),
\qquad \alpha_e<\beta_e.
\]
Segment containment is equivalent to one of the two orientations
\[
b_i(h_e)\le\alpha_e<\beta_e\le b_j(h_e)
\quad\hbox{or}\quad
b_j(h_e)\le\alpha_e<\beta_e\le b_i(h_e).
\]
Enumerate these choices on the four cells.  For a fixed orientation \(\sigma\), all constraints on a particular \(b_i\) are precisely: membership in the probability simplex, membership in its two incident observable lines, and the two oriented endpoint halfspaces.  There are no inequalities involving two unfixed vertices after the orientation is chosen.  Hence the endpoint fiber on that chart is exactly
\[
I_1(\sigma)\times I_2(\sigma)\times I_3(\sigma)\times I_4(\sigma).
\]
Two affine lines either have empty intersection, one intersection point, or coincide.  In the coincident case, simplex and endpoint halfspaces cut the common line into a closed interval.  Gaussian elimination and scalar linear inequalities therefore make every \(I_i(\sigma)\) empty, a point, or a closed interval whose endpoints are rational expressions in the entries of \(T\).  There are at most \(2^4\) orientations, proving the asserted finite union.

It remains to characterize target constancy.  Let
\[
\mu_e=\sum_zT_e(\cdot,z),
\qquad
q_{ei}=\sum_z a_{ei}(z).
\]
Since \(\sum_zv_e(z)=1\),
\[
\mu_e=q_{ei}b_i+(1-q_{ei})b_j.
\]
Rank two rules out \(q_{ei}=0\) and \(q_{ei}=1\), so \(\mu_e\) is strictly between the endpoints.  In an affine coordinate \(x=h_e(b)\),
\[
q_{ei}=\frac{x_j-x_{\mu}}{x_j-x_i}.
\]
With one endpoint fixed, this is strictly monotone in the other endpoint throughout the oriented feasible interval: its denominator never vanishes and its numerator is nonzero.  Consequently, a nondegenerate \(I_1(\sigma)\) changes the type-\(2\) weight in cell \(11\), a nondegenerate \(I_4(\sigma)\) changes the type-\(2\) weight in cell \(00\), and a nondegenerate \(I_2(\sigma)\) changes at least the type-\(2\) weight in cell \(11\).  Because the chart is a Cartesian product, the other endpoints can be held fixed during each variation.  Thus \(\tau_C\) is constant on a nonempty chart if and only if \(I_1(\sigma),I_2(\sigma),I_4(\sigma)\) are all singletons.  The interval for type \(3\) is irrelevant to both coordinates of \(\tau_C\).

Global constancy is equivalent to chartwise constancy plus equality of the finitely many chart constants.  If either test fails, choose two endpoint tuples differing in the relevant interval, or one tuple from each of two disagreeing charts.  Scalar interval endpoints and rational interior parameters yield exact choices over the ordered field generated by \(T\); the barycentric formula above yields their nonnegative coefficients.  The cycle-to-SCM lift then gives two legal full SCMs with the same \((p,m)\) and different targets.  This also proves the stated certificate claim.

Fix \((b,a)\in\mathcal C_A(T)\), a baseline \(z_0\), and a positive projective vector \(\rho\) with \(\rho_{z_0}=1\).  For positive margins \(m\), set
\[
h_i(z)=\sum_{e:i\in\mathcal I_e}m_ea_{ei}(z).
\]
The response-level shared-\(Z\) equations are \(h_i(z)=\pi_i g(z)\).  If \(g(z)/g(z_0)=\rho_z\), subtracting \(\rho_z h_i(z_0)\) gives, for the two cells \(e,f\) incident to type \(i\),
\[
m_eD^{\mathrm{res}}_{ei}(\rho)+m_fD^{\mathrm{res}}_{fi}(\rho)=0. \tag{1}
\]
Since \(m_e,m_f>0\), equation (1) has exactly the following possibilities.  Both residuals are zero; exactly one is zero, which is impossible; or both are nonzero and
\[
D^{\mathrm{res}}_{fi}(\rho)
=-\frac{m_e}{m_f}D^{\mathrm{res}}_{ei}(\rho).
\]
Thus the nonzero vectors are negatively proportional, and any nonzero coordinate determines the positive ratio \(m_f/m_e\).  Equality of the ratios obtained from different coordinates is exactly the vanishing of all corresponding two-by-two minors, together with the required opposite-sign pivot inequality.

Regard cells as vertices and response types as links.  The incidence graph is the four-cycle \(11-01-10-00-11\).  Along an active link the preceding ratio fixes the masses at its endpoints.  The product of directed ratios around an active cycle is one because the actual mass ratios telescope.  Every proper subgraph of a four-cycle is a forest, and on each of its connected components all masses are fixed up to one positive scale.  Conversely, if the local residual alternatives hold and the product is one whenever all four links are active, choose one positive root mass in every forest component and propagate the prescribed ratios.  Cycle consistency makes the propagated value path independent.  Finally choose positive component scales and normalize them so that \(\sum_em_e=1\).  The resulting margins satisfy (1) at every response type; zero-residual links impose no further restriction.  This proves the necessity and sufficiency of the residual-forest rules.

For the converse construction, equation (1) says
\[
h_i(z)=\rho_z h_i(z_0)\qquad(i=1,2,3,4;\ z\in\mathcal Z).
\]
Let \(R=\sum_z\rho_z\).  Using \(\sum_z\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_e}a_{ei}(z)=1\) and \(\sum_em_e=1\),
\[
1=\sum_{i,z}h_i(z)=R\sum_i h_i(z_0).
\]
Therefore
\[
g(z)=\frac{\rho_z}{R},
\qquad
\pi_i=R h_i(z_0)
\]
are respectively a strictly positive probability vector and a nonnegative probability vector, and they satisfy \(h_i(z)=\pi_i g(z)\).  This remains valid when a response type has zero mass.

Finally, under the reconstructed common \(g\),
\[
q^X_z=\sum_{e:e_X=1}m_e\sum_{i\in\mathcal I_e}a_{ei}(z)
=P(X=1,Z=z),
\qquad g(z)=P(Z=z).
\]
Because every \(g(z)>0\), \(Z\perp X\) holds if and only if all projective ratios \(q^X_z/g(z)\) are equal, equivalently if and only if
\[
q^X_zg(z')=q^X_{z'}g(z)
\quad\hbox{for every }z,z'.
\]
Its negation is precisely the relevance inequality in \(\mathcal C_B(T)\).  The cycle-to-SCM lift then proves that the residual rules plus this inequality are also sufficient for a legal design-B SCM.

On the experimental submodel, \(S=1\) gives \(m=r\), and randomization gives \(P(U=i\mid X=x)=\pi_i\).  The cited 2023 theorem identifies the four response-type probabilities and makes its plug-in estimator consistent.  We now verify that its observable conditions also pin the larger cycle fiber, rather than merely the restricted experimental parameterization.

For a cell \(e=(x,y)\) and a proxy category \(w\), the determinant of the paper's \(2\)-by-\(2\) matrix \(Q_{xyw}\), after factoring out the positive cell probability twice, is
\[
\det\begin{pmatrix}
1&P(W=w\mid E=e)\\
P(Z=z_1\mid E=e)&P(W=w,Z=z_1\mid E=e)
\end{pmatrix}.
\]
For any two-component cycle factorization of that cell, direct expansion gives
\[
\det(Q_{xyw})=K_e\{b_i(w)-b_j(w)\}, \tag{1}
\]
where \(K_e\ne0\) does not depend on \(w\); nonvanishing follows from Condition (3).  Hence the determinant ratios in the paper are observable direction ratios for the affine line \(\mathcal L_e\).  The four inequalities in Condition (3) say exactly that the two incident directions used in each of equations (8)--(11) are distinct.  Those displayed equations are nonsingular two-by-two linear systems for the corresponding coordinates of the common endpoint.  Thus every \(T_e\) has rank two and, for each response type \(i\), its two incident observable lines meet in the unique point \(b_i\) recovered by those equations.

Apply the rank-two orientation theorem.  On every nonempty orientation chart, every endpoint interval is the singleton consisting of that incident-line intersection.  Therefore the whole \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) has one endpoint tuple and one coefficient tuple, and its target agrees with the generating experimental SCM.  In the paper's ordering, types \((00,01,10,11)\) correspond to the present types \((4,2,3,1)\), so
\[
\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}=(\pi_4,\pi_2,\pi_3,\pi_1).
\]
Response consistency and randomization then give
\[
\mathrm{PN}
=\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_1+\pi_2}
=\frac{\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}{\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2+\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_4},
\qquad
\mathrm{PS}
=\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_2+\pi_4}
=\frac{\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}{\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_1+\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}_2}.
\]
The positive observed cells make both denominators positive.  This proves
\(\mathcal T_A(p,r)=\{\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}})\}\).  The all-rank-two branch is one of the oriented charts in the definition of \(\mathscr A\), so it returns this value.  By the cited plug-in consistency and continuity of \(\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}\) at positive denominators,
\[
\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\widehat\pi_n^{\mathrm{SK}})
\xrightarrow{P}\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}).
\]

We next check the boundary datum directly.  Each listed \(b_i^{\mathrm{bd}}\) is strictly positive and normalized.  In every cell, the two coefficient rows are nonnegative, have columnwise sum \(v_e=(1/3,1/3,1/3)\), and are not proportional.  The two incident endpoint columns are distinct, so
\[
\operatorname{rank}(T_e^{\mathrm{bd}})=2.
\]
At every \((w,z)\), at least one coefficient is positive and every endpoint coordinate is positive; hence every entry of \(T_e^{\mathrm{bd}}\), and therefore of \(p^{\mathrm{bd}}\), is positive.  Moreover
\[
\sum_es_e^{\mathrm{bd}}m_e^{\mathrm{bd}}
=\frac14\left(\frac18+\frac14+\frac38+\frac12\right)
=\frac5{16},
\]
and cell by cell
\[
\frac{s_e^{\mathrm{bd}}m_e^{\mathrm{bd}}}{5/16}=r_e^{\mathrm{bd}}.
\]
The cycle lift therefore gives \(\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing\).

In simplex coordinates, the relevant lines are
\[
\mathcal L_{11}=\mathcal L_{00}=\{b:b(w_2)=1/5\},
\quad
\mathcal L_{01}=\{b:b(w_1)=1/5\},
\quad
\mathcal L_{10}=\{b:b(w_3)=1/5\}.
\]
Thus the transverse intersections pin \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_3^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  In cell \(11\), the normalized columns at \(z_1,z_3\) are respectively \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}},b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\), so the segment condition forces the type-\(2\) endpoint to lie at or beyond \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\) away from \(b_1^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  In cell \(00\), those columns are \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}},b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\), so the same endpoint must lie at or beyond \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\) away from \(b_4^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  The two closed half-line constraints meet only at \(b_2^{\mathrm{bd}}\).  All four endpoints, and hence all rank-two coefficients, are therefore fixed.  In particular the four displayed zero coefficients are compulsory, and
\[
\tau_C
=\left(0+\frac16+\frac13,\frac13+\frac16+0\right)
=\left(\frac12,\frac12\right).
\]
The rank-two theorem and the cycle lift prove the asserted singleton full-SCM target set.

The same argument is stable relative to the support face that retains the four indicated zero positions: the zero columns continue to expose the common endpoint, the strict endpoint order and the two transverse intersections remain strict conditions, and all other displayed probabilities remain positive.  These are relatively open inequalities, and the displayed datum is a member, so that chart is nonempty and rigid.  Finally \(r^{\mathrm{bd}}\ne m^{\mathrm{bd}}\), whereas \(S=1\) almost surely would imply \(r=m\); hence this datum is outside the no-selection experimental submodel.

Outcome-dependent selection makes \(s_e=P_{\vartheta}(S=1\mid E=e)\) well defined as a function of \(e\) alone.  When every \(s_e>0\), Bayes' identity gives
\[
r_e=P_{\vartheta}(E=e\mid S=1)
=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(S=1\mid E=e)P_{\vartheta}(E=e)}{P_{\vartheta}(S=1)}
=\frac{s_em_e}{c}.
\]
Thus \(m_e=cr_e/s_e\).  Summing over \(e\) and using \(\sum_em_e=1\) yields
\[
c^{-1}=\sum_{f\in\mathcal E}\frac{r_f}{s_f},
\qquad
m_e=\frac{r_e/s_e}{\sum_{f\in\mathcal E}r_f/s_f}.
\]
All divisions are legitimate by selected-table positivity and the assumed positivity of \(s_e\).  In the IV-plus-proxy construction, \(m\) is otherwise a nuisance coordinate of \(\mathcal C_B(T)\); known selection therefore imposes exactly this additional equality, which is the stated intersection.

Write \(\pi_i=P_{\vartheta}(U=i)\).  Response consistency and \(X\perp U\) give
\[
P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)=\pi_1+\pi_2,
\qquad
P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)=\pi_1+\pi_3=\pi_1,
\]
where the last equality uses \(P_{\vartheta}(U=3)=0\).  Therefore the risk difference is \(\pi_2\).  The events \((X,Y)=(1,1)\) and \((X,Y)=(0,0)\) have positive probability because \(S=1\) and the selected table is positive, so the following divisions are legitimate.  Again by randomization and response consistency,
\[
\mathrm{PN}
=P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=1,Y=1)
=\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_1+\pi_2}
=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)},
\]
and
\[
\mathrm{PS}
=P_{\vartheta}(U=2\mid X=0,Y=0)
=\frac{\pi_2}{\pi_2+\pi_4}
=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)}.
\]
This calculation applies to every SCM in the restricted randomized monotone submodel.  If the unrestricted target set \(\mathcal T_A(p,m)\) is a singleton and contains the displayed \(\vartheta\), its sole element must equal \(\tau(\vartheta)\), so it equals the same pair.  No rigidity of the unrestricted fiber was inferred from randomization and monotonicity alone.

added_lemmas.statement: In the no-selection randomized experimental response-type model with positive observed cells, \(W\perp Z\mid U\), and Conditions (1)--(3) of Shingaki--Kuroki (2023), the four response-type probabilities are identified.  Their equations (8)--(13) give plug-in estimators of those probabilities, and their asymptotic-normality result implies consistency whenever the empirical cell probabilities obey the multinomial law of large numbers.

added_lemmas.statement: Under the recursive IV-plus-proxy factorization and conditions (i)--(iii) of Kawakami (2021), Theorem 1, the four joint probabilities of the binary potential-outcome types are identified.  The proof on pages 12135--12137 recovers the treatment-conditional response-type weights by simultaneous linear equations, and these weights determine PN and PS.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Suppose locally that \(S=1\) almost surely, \(X\perp U\) under \(P_{\vartheta}\), and \(P_{\vartheta}(U=3)=0\).  Within the submodel in which these restrictions are imposed on every compatible SCM, the causal targets satisfy
\[
\mathrm{PN}=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)},
\qquad
\mathrm{PS}=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)}.
\]
If, in addition, the unrestricted full fiber \(\mathcal T_A(p,m)\) is a singleton and contains this \(\vartheta\), its unique value equals the same pair.  The three local restrictions are not conditions on either main design.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The original wording incorrectly makes local randomization and monotonicity imply rigidity of the larger unrestricted proxy fiber.  A counterexample takes uniform proxies, randomized treatment, no type 3, and response weights \(1/5,3/10,0,1/2\): every observed cell is positive, but rank-one proxy tables admit arbitrary incident splits and hence different PN/PS values.  The corrected claim states the classical formula on the restricted submodel and only asserts agreement with the unrestricted fiber when that fiber is independently rigid.

proposed.statement:
On the local no-selection experimental submodel \(S=1\) almost surely and \(X\perp(U,W,Z)\), impose \(W\perp Z\mid U\) and Conditions (1)--(3) of Theorem 1 of Shingaki--Kuroki (2023). After the label conversion \(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}}=(\pi_4,\pi_2,\pi_3,\pi_1)\), \(\mathcal T_A(p,r)=\{\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}})\}\), the exact value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals this singleton, and \(\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\widehat\pi_n^{\mathrm{SK}})\xrightarrow{P}\phi_{\mathrm{SK}}(\pi^{\mathrm{SK}})\). As a separate boundary-coverage check, for \(|\mathcal W|=|\mathcal Z|=3\), the explicit datum \((b^{\mathrm{bd}},a^{\mathrm{bd}},T^{\mathrm{bd}},r^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}},s^{\mathrm{bd}},p^{\mathrm{bd}})\) has \(\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})
e\varnothing\), \(\operatorname{rank}(T^{\mathrm{bd}}_e)=2\) for all \(e\), \(\mathcal L_{11}=\mathcal L_{00}\) when \(T=T^{\mathrm{bd}}\), compulsory zeros \(a^{\mathrm{bd}}_{11,1}(z_3)=a^{\mathrm{bd}}_{11,2}(z_1)=a^{\mathrm{bd}}_{00,2}(z_3)=a^{\mathrm{bd}}_{00,4}(z_1)=0\), and \(\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}\). proposed.statement:
Suppose locally that \(S=1\) almost surely, \(X\perp U\) under \(P_{\vartheta}\), and \(P_{\vartheta}(U=3)=0\).  Within the submodel in which these restrictions are imposed on every compatible SCM, the causal targets satisfy
\[
\mathrm{PN}=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)},
\qquad
\mathrm{PS}=\frac{P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=1)-P_{\vartheta}(Y=1\mid X=0)}{P_{\vartheta}(Y=0\mid X=0)}.
\]
If, in addition, the unrestricted full fiber \(\mathcal T_A(p,m)\) is a singleton and contains this \(\vartheta\), its unique value equals the same pair.  The three local restrictions are not conditions on either main design.
proposed.justification: This is a validation reduction to the classical randomized monotone formulas, while explicitly separating that restricted identification statement from rigidity of the larger full proxy fiber.
proposed.gap: The elementary response-type calculation is classical; the needed correction is to avoid importing local randomization and monotonicity into every point of the unrestricted fiber.
proposed.consumer: Implementers can use the classical formulas as a regression test only on the restricted submodel, or compare them with a separately certified unrestricted singleton.

proposed.statement: On every observable law satisfying Conditions 2--3 of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026), the rigid value returned by \(\mathscr A\) equals the PN/PS value obtained from their Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33). The same atlas is defined on additional singular and boundary observable laws not covered by those regular conditions, including design-A support-face strata with rank loss, coincident endpoints, inactive rows, or forced-zero incident coefficients and analogous design-B strata governed by response-level shared-\(Z\) residual forests. On each such law, the full-rigidity theorem returns either a target-rigidity certificate with an exact value or a legal target-changing full-SCM certificate.
proposed.justification: This supporting result validates agreement with the anchor formulas on their regular domain and records the singular and boundary domains handled by the atlas.
proposed.gap: The 2026 anchor supplies regular inversion formulas but does not state a full-fiber decision procedure on singular support faces or residual-forest boundary strata.
proposed.consumer: Users of the anchor formulas can verify numerical agreement on regular tables and obtain a defined certification workflow when regular inversions are unavailable.

proposed.statement: For every \(\vartheta\in\mathcal F_B(p)\) in the no-selection overlap satisfying \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}(P_{\vartheta})\), the simultaneous equations in the proof of Kawakami (2021), Theorem 1 on pages 12135--12137 identify \(\omega_0^{\mathrm K}\) and \(\omega_1^{\mathrm K}\). If \(\mathcal T_B(p)\) is a singleton, its atlas value agrees with \(\tau(\vartheta)=\phi_{\mathrm K}(\omega_0^{\mathrm K},\omega_1^{\mathrm K})\). Kawakami's identified scope is the four joint probabilities of binary potential-outcome types, together with their treatment-conditional weights used for PN and PS, under Figure 2(b), equation (2), and Theorem 1(i)--(iii). For the single explicit selected boundary datum \((p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\), \(\mathcal F_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})\ne\varnothing\) and \(\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}\), but \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is singular for each \(x\): because \(\mathcal W=\{w_1,w_2,w_3\}\), its first column is the sum of its last three columns. Thus this legal selected response-cycle law violates the named invertibility assumption in Kawakami's Theorem 1(i) while remaining classified by the atlas; this is a strict scope separation, not a subsumption claim.
proposed.justification: This supporting theorem records the exact no-selection IV-plus-proxy overlap and a one-law separation from Kawakami's regular invertibility domain.
proposed.gap: Kawakami (2021), Figure 2(b), equation (2), Theorem 1(i)--(iii), and its appendix identify all four response-type probabilities under invertible proxy-loading and observable blocks plus cross-treatment separation, but do not classify selected or singular response-cycle fibers.

open_obligations.what_is_open: An exhaustive response-cycle classification for every simultaneous rank-one, equal-endpoint, inactive-row, support-face, and IV residual pattern, including agreement across all real components, without a generic two-copy quantifier-elimination classifier.
open_obligations.obstruction: Rank-two segments and residual forest ratios do not control hidden split vectors on equal-endpoint rank-one cells.  With several inactive rows, endpoint propagation can stop, and lower-dimensional components can meet across faces with different target images.  The supplied draft explicitly has no exhaustion or gluing proof for these patterns.
open_obligations.attempted: Oriented rank-two boxes, distinct-endpoint projective transfers, a complete one-rank-one chart, residual-ratio forest propagation, exact mixed rational instances, and a cubic algebraic IV completion were checked.  These tests establish branches but do not enumerate every incidence geometry.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The closed part of the classification consists of two exact reductions.  When all four cells have rank two, the endpoint fiber is the union of at most \(2^4\) orientation boxes, and target constancy is equivalent to singleton intervals for response types \(1,2,4\) plus equality across boxes.  For every fixed cycle factorization in design B, positive unknown margins exist exactly under the residual proportionality, forest propagation, and active-cycle product conditions proved above.  The supplied exact regression additionally verifies a one-rank-one, three-rank-two chart and exhibits an algebraic design-B completion with projective coordinate equal to the isolated root in \((1,101/100)\) of
\[
45218q^3+108487q^2-278050q+124258=0.
\]
What remains unproved is an exhaustive structural propagation and gluing argument when several rank-one cells, equal endpoints, inactive incident rows, and residual support faces occur simultaneously.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Necessity and sufficiency of the claimed finite structural atlas on arbitrary mixed-support fibers.
open_obligations.obstruction: This theorem depends directly on the unresolved mixed-support OEQ.  Generic semialgebraic two-copy decision would establish decidability but would violate the theorem's promised causal-specific classifier and would not prove that the stated structural charts are exhaustive.
open_obligations.attempted: The full SCM lift, all-rank-two orientation classification, IV residual-margin elimination, and exact boundary regressions were proved or verified.
open_obligations.partial_result: The cycle-to-SCM lift proves that any target disagreement in \(\mathcal C_A(T)\) or \(\mathcal C_B(T)\) yields legal full-SCM twins, including boundary mechanisms.  The all-rank-two design-A branch and the conditional design-B residual-margin problem have exact necessary-and-sufficient tests.  Hence the claimed full theorem is established on those branches, but not on arbitrary mixed-support fibers: the missing mixed-support elimination is exactly the step needed to show that the proposed finite chart list exhausts every real component and support face.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Coverage of every singular and boundary observable law by the same global atlas.
open_obligations.obstruction: Regular-formula agreement follows from the published identification result and target preservation, but the universal boundary clause is precisely the still-unproved mixed-support exhaustiveness claim.
open_obligations.attempted: The 2026 source was checked at Theorem 1 and Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33); all-rank-two forced-zero boundaries and the conditional IV residual problem were separated and proved.
open_obligations.partial_result: On the regular domain of Shingaki--Yoshida--Kuroki (2026), their Appendix equations (A.28)--(A.33) identify the same conditional response-type probabilities that equal \(\tau_C\) under the cycle-to-SCM map.  Therefore, whenever the corresponding full cycle fiber is rigid, its singleton must agree with the published formula.  Independently of the unfinished mixed atlas, the all-rank-two theorem certifies forced-zero assignment boundaries such as the explicit \(p^{\mathrm{bd}}\) datum, and the residual-forest theorem exactly handles unknown design-B margins conditional on a cycle factorization.  Exhaustive coverage of every rank-loss and inactive-row law still requires the unresolved mixed-support classification.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The claim that the unfinished global atlas returns the unique design-B value on every Kawakami-regular overlap law.
open_obligations.obstruction: Kawakami's simultaneous equations and the explicit singular-matrix separation are verified, but attributing the unique value to the global compiler still requires the unresolved full-atlas theorem.
open_obligations.attempted: The publisher theorem and proof were checked; the PN/PS transformation and the explicit column-dependence calculation were derived directly.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Kawakami (2021), Theorem 1, identifies the treatment-conditional response-type weights under the predicate \(\mathcal K_{\mathrm K}\).  Response consistency then gives directly
\[
\tau(\vartheta)=\phi_{\mathrm K}(\omega_0^{\mathrm K},\omega_1^{\mathrm K}).
\]
For the explicit boundary endpoints, each row of \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) has first coordinate one and last three coordinates summing to one.  Hence its first column is the sum of its last three columns and \(A_x^{\mathrm K}(b^{\mathrm{bd}})\) is singular for both treatment values.  The preceding boundary proof gives \(\mathcal T_A(p^{\mathrm{bd}},m^{\mathrm{bd}})=\{(1/2,1/2)\}\).  Thus the stated one-law scope separation is proved.  The remaining phrase about the value returned by the global atlas still depends on completion of that atlas.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A termination and certificate-size proof for the specific structural compiler rather than for generic real quantifier elimination.
open_obligations.obstruction: The compiler whose chart count and algebraic degrees are to be bounded has not been completed.  A CAD bound for the raw two-copy formula cannot certify the promised structural chart enumeration.
open_obligations.attempted: The fixed-alphabet variable and degree counts and the rational all-rank-two algorithm were bounded; the residual forest reduces the margin block explicitly.
open_obligations.partial_result: For fixed \(k=|\mathcal Z|\) and \(\ell=|\mathcal W|\), the raw cycle fibers are semialgebraic with \(O(k\ell+k+\ell)\) equations and inequalities of degree at most two in \(O(k+\ell)\) latent coordinates after the redundant endpoint rows are eliminated.  Generic real-algebraic decision and sampling would therefore terminate with a doubly exponential fixed-alphabet envelope, and the all-rank-two structural branch already terminates using only linear algebra and order tests over \(\mathbb K_{\zeta}\).  This does not prove the stated theorem, because that theorem specifically attributes the bound and extraction guarantees to the unfinished structural compiler and forbids substituting the generic two-copy decision predicate.

open_obligations.what_is_open: Unconditional selector correctness for the claimed atlas on every separated rigid stratum.
open_obligations.obstruction: The delta-method calculation closes conditional on local atlas exhaustiveness, but an omitted mixed-support chart could invalidate the certification and incompatibility-distance step.
open_obligations.attempted: The multinomial covariance, chart-distance rate, common-Jacobian Taylor expansion, sandwich consistency, and fallback behavior were derived conditionally.
open_obligations.partial_result:
Conditional on local exhaustiveness of the certified atlas, the separated-stratum calculation is standard and explicit.  Independent multinomial sampling gives
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)\Rightarrow N(0,\Omega_{\zeta}),
\qquad
\widehat\Omega_n\xrightarrow{P}\Omega_{\zeta}.
\]
For every incident chart, the distance inequality
\(d_{\chi}(\widehat\zeta_n)\le\|\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta\|_2=O_P(n^{-1/2})\) and \(t_n=n^{-1/4}\) make the distance test pass, while continuity and \(\eta_{\chi}(\zeta)\ge\varepsilon\) make the slack test pass.  The distance separation excludes incompatible charts.  Common values and Jacobians on incident charts, followed by a Taylor expansion, yield
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_n-\tau)
=J_{\chi}(\zeta)\sqrt n(\widehat\zeta_n-\zeta)+o_P(1),
\]
and hence covariance \(V_{\tau}\); positive definiteness and plug-in continuity give the Wald conclusion.  What is not yet available is the global compiler theorem that certifies the incident set and excludes an omitted mixed-support chart.

open_obligations.what_is_open: The uniform first-order Hausdorff equivalence between the exact profile confidence fiber and the selected Wald ellipse on the globally defined atlas.
open_obligations.obstruction: Finite-sample coverage is exact without the atlas, but the Hausdorff assertion requires a uniform quadratic profile expansion over all incident glued charts and proof that the compiler omits no nearby mixed-support component.
open_obligations.attempted: Berger--Boos coverage was proved by the preliminary-region event and exact super-uniform tail values; the regular local quadratic reduction was derived conditional on atlas exhaustiveness.
open_obligations.partial_result:
The finite-sample coverage part does not require rank stability.  Let \(q_0\) be the true observable law and \(t_0=\tau(\vartheta)\).  Inversion of each binomial tail makes its two-sided Clopper--Pearson interval miss its true cell probability with probability no greater than its allocated error.  Bonferroni therefore gives
\[
P_{q_0}(q_0\notin C_n)\le\beta_n.
\]
For fixed \((q,t)\) with \(t\in\mathcal T(q)\), the exact upper-tail randomization value
\[
G_{q,t}=P_q\{\Delta_n^{\mathrm{rep}}(t)\ge\Delta_n^{\mathrm{obs}}(t)\}
\]
is super-uniform under \(q\): for every \(u\in[0,1]\), \(P_q(G_{q,t}\le u)\le u\), including at atoms.  On \(\{q_0\in C_n\}\), the supremum defining \(\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)\) contains \(q_0\), so
\[
\operatorname{pv}_n(t_0)\ge\min\{1,\beta_n+G_{q_0,t_0}\}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
P_{q_0}\{t_0\notin K_n\}
\le P_{q_0}(q_0\notin C_n)+P_{q_0}(G_{q_0,t_0}\le\alpha-\beta_n)
\le\beta_n+(\alpha-\beta_n)=\alpha.
\]
This proves exact coverage, uniformly along arbitrary transition sequences.  On a locally exhaustive separated smooth chart, a quadratic multinomial likelihood expansion and the common incident Jacobian reduce the profile deviance to the Wald quadratic up to \(o_P(1)\), which would imply \(\sqrt n,d_{\mathrm H}(K_n,W_n)\to0\).  The unresolved part is a uniform glued-chart profile expansion after proving that no mixed-support component is omitted by the compiler.

open_obligations.partial_result:
The imposed positive selection probabilities determine the application margin, without approximation, by
\[
m_e^{\mathrm G}
=\frac{r_e^{\mathrm G}/s_e^{\mathrm G}}{\sum_f r_f^{\mathrm G}/s_f^{\mathrm G}}.
\]
Thus any eventual audit must intersect the design-B residual equations with this fixed margin and must test relevance separately.  The frozen core does not supply the numerical released count table or the binarization thresholds needed to determine \(p^{\mathrm G}\), and the exhaustive mixed-support compiler needed to classify its exact fiber is not yet proved.  No compatibility, rigidity, or legal-twin conclusion for the named data can therefore be derived from the supplied primitives.
